- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 1–3%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in the following 5–10 days; apply a downward correction of 2–5% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.4) and price is trending down, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 1–3% to reflect mean reversion toward lower range.
- Model frequently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon (especially days 1–7), especially when sentiment is neutral or positive; apply a 1–2% downward bias to first 5 days.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.4–0.8) and price is volatile, model tends to smooth out extremes; consider adding a 0.5–1.5% volatility buffer to forecast extremes.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.80+ values, model may be overconfident; reduce forecast variance by 10–20% to reflect diminishing momentum.
